title: About my Father's business (Luke 2:41–52)
hook: he grew in wisdom and stature and in favor with God and people

segments.voice: Yesterday, Anna, who prayed night and day and told everyone who was waiting. Your line was she never stopped.

A whole day's walk out of Jerusalem, Mary and Joseph realize their son isn't with them. They supposed him to be in the company, Luke says, traveling home from the Passover with relatives and friends. So nobody worried, until they looked among the kinsfolk and acquaintance, and he wasn't there. A parent who has lost sight of a child at a mall or a beach knows that cold drop in the stomach. They turn back and search the city. One day. Two days. On the third day they find him, and Luke tells us exactly where.
screen: `A DAY'S WALK, AND HE'S NOT THERE.`

segments.voice: In the King James Bible, "after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions." Doctors here means teachers, scholars of the law. And notice the order: hearing first, then asking. Mary speaks first: "Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." He answers with the first words Luke ever gives him: "How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The Greek is shorter, something like in the things of my Father, and some translations say in my Father's house. Either way, he names God as Father, while Joseph stands right there. Luke adds, honestly, that his parents didn't understand. Then he goes home with them to Nazareth, and Luke says he was subject unto them: the boy who knew whose house he was in still does as his parents ask. Then the verse that closes the chapter: "And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man." Christians believe Jesus was the Son of God, and Luke still says he grew: in learning, in height, in the trust of the people around him. Luke writes the growing down as part of the story. And Mary "kept all these sayings in her heart." She didn't understand yet. She kept it anyway.
screen: then, large: `JESUS INCREASED IN WISDOM AND STATURE.`

segments.voice: Picture the boy in the temple, listening among people who knew more than he did, and then the four ways Luke says he grew: wisdom, stature, favor with God, favor with people. Let one rise to the top for you, something to understand better, your body or your sleep, your prayer or your quiet, a relationship that could be kinder, and choose the smallest possible step in it. If you pray, ask to grow the way Luke says Jesus grew; if not, simply choose your step.
Wist. An old word for knew, from Jesus' first recorded words: wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
Your line: growing is holy. Even Luke's Jesus increased, a little at a time. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Christians read Luke 2:52 as a picture of whole-person growth, and the finding in the temple is remembered as one of the five Joyful Mysteries of the Catholic rosary.

notes: Greek of 2:49 (en tois tou patros mou) read as 'my Father's house' or 'my Father's affairs'. Confirm phrasing.
helikia can mean age or stature (standard lexicons). Confirm.
Travel in large kinship caravans to and from festivals is a common historical reconstruction from 2:44; keep it light.
'The only story the Gospels tell between his infancy and adulthood' refers to the canonical Gospels. Reviewer edit: now 'the four Gospels'. Confirm wording.
Reviewer edit: the review no longer calls Anna 'eighty-four years old', since day 511 treats Luke 2:37 as ambiguous (age 84 or 84 years a widow).
'A carpenter's household' draws on Mark 6:3 / Matthew 13:55; Luke 2 itself does not name Joseph's trade.
